properties.name: Tall el-Hammam (TeH)
properties.location: E Jordan Valley / NE Dead Sea plain, Jordan (~31.84 N, 35.67 E)
properties.hypothesis: Steven Collins and others identified TeH as biblical Sodom (Gen 13–19; cities of the Kikkar). Bunch et al. (Sci Rep 2021) argued a ~1650 BCE Tunguska-scale cosmic airburst destroyed the Middle Bronze city and could underlie the Genesis 19 fire-from-heaven tradition.
properties.found: A large MBA settlement with a destruction/abandonment horizon and reports of heat-affected pottery/mudbrick and unusual materials. The 2021 paper claimed shocked quartz, melts >2000 °C, spherules, salt spike, skeletal trauma, and regional abandonment.
properties.divergence: Scientific Reports retracted the airburst article on 24 Apr 2025 (doi:10.1038/s41598-025-99265-5), citing Jaret & Harris (mineralogy/geochemistry not impact-diagnostic) and Boslough & Bruno (invalid Tunguska comparisons). Editors: airburst destruction 'not sufficiently supported.' Sodom ID was never mainstream consensus. Some coauthors disagree and republished elsewhere; Nature Portfolio retraction stands. Pattern (C) lab claim retracted; (A/B) place ID contested.
properties.sources: Bunch et al. Sci Rep 2021 doi:10.1038/s41598-021-97778-3 (RETRACTED); Retraction Note doi:10.1038/s41598-025-99265-5; Jaret & Harris Sci Rep 2022 doi:10.1038/s41598-022-08216-x; Boslough & Bruno Sci Rep 2025 doi:10.1038/s41598-025-98362-9; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-99265-5; Jerusalem Post coverage of retraction; Bunch et al. properties.notes: Fair: TeH is a real excavated MBA city with destruction evidence. The airburst mechanism and Genesis-Sodom equation are what failed peer confidence. Distinguish site archaeology from the retracted bolide paper. Surveyor type (C).

properties.name: Jericho (Tell es-Sultan)
properties.location: West Bank / Jordan Valley, near modern Jericho
properties.hypothesis: Joshua 6: Israelites march around fortified Jericho; walls fall; city burned. John Garstang (1930s) dated City IV fiery destruction ~1400 BCE and linked it to the conquest.  Intifada halted the Italian–Palestinian season: Sapienza’s Tell es-Sultan team records that autumn 2000 fieldwork was interrupted by the severe political situation, with a forced field stop into the mid-2000s before cooperation digs returned—proof that Jericho’s trenches track geopolitics as well as stratigraphy.
properties.found: Major Bronze Age destruction with collapsed mudbrick, ash, and stored grain. Kenyon redated Garstang's City IV walls/destruction to end of Middle Bronze (~1550 BCE), with only sparse LB occupation—not a walled Late Bronze city matching a ~13th-c. conquest model.
properties.divergence: Mainstream view: Kenyon's MB end dating (supported by later 14C) means the famous destruction is too early for a Late Bronze 'conquest' horizon; no fortified city fitting ~1230 BCE. Minority (Wood et al.) revive Garstang ~1400 BCE pottery reading. Debate continues but Kenyon's stratigraphy dominates textbooks. Pattern (A): real place and real destruction; dating/interpretation overreach relative to popular conquest sync.
properties.sources: Garstang & Garstang, The Story of Jericho (1948); Kenyon, Digging Up Jericho (1957); Wood, BAR 16/2 (1990); Bruins & van der Plicht Radiocarbon 1995; NatGeo 'Fall of Jericho' summary; MDPI Religions 14/796 (2023 overview); Expedition Bible note C27CmsSGx5Y (Jericho Unearthed — Garstang vs Kenyon); https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C27CmsSGx5Y; K. Kenyon, Digging Up Jericho; J. Garstang, The Story of Jericho (1948)
properties.notes: Not 'no Jericho'—site is Tell es-Sultan. Contest is chronology and whether Joshua's narrative matches a specific destruction layer. Surveyor type (A).

properties.name: Ai — et-Tell vs Khirbet el-Maqatir (and Kh. Nisya)
properties.location: Central highlands N of Jerusalem (et-Tell ~9 mi N; Maqatir ~0.6 mi W of et-Tell)
properties.hypothesis: Joshua 7–8: Israelites attack Ai near Bethel after Jericho. W.F. Albright (1924) fixed Ai at et-Tell; expected LB fortified town destroyed by fire.
properties.found: et-Tell: major Early Bronze city, then gap—unoccupied in Late Bronze at the conventional conquest horizon. Callaway called Ai an 'embarrassment' to conquest models that take both Bible and et-Tell ID seriously. ABR reports an LB I fortified site with destruction at Maqatir.
properties.divergence: Classic wrong-site vs alt-ID problem: if et-Tell = Ai, archaeology diverges from Joshua 7–8 at the conquest horizon. Conservatives propose Maqatir (or formerly Nisya) as the true Ai. Majority scholarship still defaults to et-Tell and treats the narrative as etiological or relocated memory. Pattern (B) primary; (A) if alternate accepted.
properties.sources: Albright JPOS 1924; Callaway, BA 1968 / excavation reports; Wood ABR reports (biblearchaeology.org); BibleInterp Maqatir 2013 PDF; Livingston Kh. Nisya publications; Expedition Bible note lK7GQxkEkKk (Problem of Ai); https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lK7GQxkEkKk; Callaway BASOR Ai reports; https://www.biblicalarchaeology.org/daily/biblical-sites-places/biblical-archaeology-places/the-great-bethsaida-debate/; Arav & Freund Bethsaida vols; Notley & Aviam reports

properties.divergence: Two competent teams, two sites—ongoing 'Great Bethsaida Debate.' Geography (shore vs inland) and Roman finds at el-Araj challenge exclusive et-Tell ID. Not a fraud case; genuine site-identification contest. Pattern (B).

properties.name: Capernaum — 'House of Peter' (Insula I)
properties.location: NW Sea of Galilee, Tell Hum / Kefar Nahum, Israel
properties.hypothesis: Mark 1:29–34; Luke 4:38–39 etc.: Jesus heals Peter's mother-in-law in Peter's house at Capernaum. Franciscan excavators expected to find the house under the octagonal Byzantine church tradition.
properties.found: First-century domestic complex under the octagonal church; one room plastered and shifted from household pottery to lamps/storage jars by late 1st/early 2nd c.—interpreted as meeting hall; 4th-c. domus ecclesiae; pilgrim graffiti naming Jesus/Peter.
properties.divergence: Site Capernaum ID is solid. Named 'Peter's house' rests on early Christian tradition + architectural special treatment, not an inscription saying 'Peter lived here.' Critics doubt continuous Jewish-Christian memory transmission. Plausible tradition ≠ archaeological proof of ownership. Pattern (A).

properties.name: Noah's Ark claims — Durupınar / Ararat region
properties.location: E Turkey: Durupınar formation near Doğubayazıt; various Ararat search locales

properties.found: Boat-shaped natural landform (Durupınar) in landslide/earthflow terrain; claimed 'wood,' 'rivets,' and chambers have not survived independent scientific verification as ship remains. Geological consensus: syncline / limestone block + clay flow shaping.

properties.name: Ebla (Tell Mardikh)
properties.location: NW Syria, ~55 km SW of Aleppo
properties.hypothesis: After palace archives found (1970s), Giovanni Pettinato announced tablet parallels to biblical patriarchs, Yahweh, Flood story, and Cities of the Plain (Sodom, Gomorrah, Zoar/Bela) per Gen 14.  War closed the tablets’ hometown: after the 2010 season, Sapienza’s Italian mission at Ebla (Tell Mardikh) suspended fieldwork from 2011 amid Syria’s conflict—years when the tell suffered military use and clandestine digging before later recovery missions returned to stabilize what survived.
properties.found: Vast 3rd-millennium BCE cuneiform archive of a major Syrian kingdom—real breakthrough for Near Eastern history. Shared Semitic personal-name patterns (e.g. forms resembling Ishmael, Michael) appear as expected in the region.
properties.divergence: Pettinato's Sodom/Gomorrah/Zoar readings contested by Archi; Pettinato himself walked back Zoar/Bela and could not substantiate five cities. Matthiae denied patriarchal proofs, Yahweh cult, and Sodom mentions in preface. Consensus: Ebla does not confirm biblical patriarchs or Cities of the Plain. Pattern (A)/(C): real archive; biblical overclaims retracted/walked back.
properties.sources: Archi, 'Are the Cities of the Plain Mentioned in the Ebla Tablets?' Biblical Archaeology Review 7/6 (1981) https://library.biblicalarchaeology.org/article/are-the-cities-of-the-plain-mentioned-in-the-ebla-tablets/; Archi BAS Library 'Are the Cities of the Plain Mentioned in the Ebla Tablets?'; Christianity Today 1981 Ebla overview; Matthiae English preface denials (1979)
properties.notes: Classic cautionary tale: sensational Bible parallels announced before tablets fully published. Surveyor type (A)/(C).

properties.divergence: Site ID largely succeeded (contrast Ai). Contests focus on syncing specific destruction layers to Abimelech (Judg 9) or Josh 24 ceremony—chronology/interpretation debates rather than 'wrong hill.' Some maximalist/minimalist fights over patriarchal historicity. Pattern (A).
properties.sources: Wright Shechem reports; ABD Shechem; BAS articles on Shechem temple; Bible Odyssey / standard encyclopedia entries
properties.notes: Included as partial contrast: Bible guided to a real capital; narrative-layer matches still argued. Surveyor type (A).

properties.name: Megiddo — 'Solomon's stables'
properties.location: Tel Megiddo, Israel
properties.hypothesis: 1 Kgs 9:15–19; 10:26 — Solomon's chariot cities. Chicago excavators labeled pillared buildings 'Solomon's stables.'
properties.found: Large pillared buildings; function debated (stables vs storehouses/barracks). Stratigraphic date shifted with low/high chronology away from automatic 10th-c. Solomon.
properties.divergence: Even if stables, many date them later (Omride or 8th c.). Name 'Solomon's stables' is a legacy label that over-determined interpretation. Pattern (A).
properties.sources: Megiddo expedition reports; Finkelstein low-chronology papers; standard Bible dictionary Megiddo entries
properties.notes: Companion to CBG-09 gates debate. Surveyor type (A).

properties.name: Khirbet Qeiyafa — 'Davidic' fortress media claims
properties.location: Shephelah overlooking Elah Valley, Israel
properties.hypothesis: 1 Sam 17 Elah Valley / early Judahite state under David. Excavators (Garfinkel) argued a fortified 10th-c. Judahite city supporting a Davidic kingdom against minimalist views.
properties.found: Short-lived fortified Iron Age site; two gates; ostracon with early Hebrew/Canaanite text; cultic rooms without figurines (interpreted as aniconic).
properties.divergence: Site is real and important; contest is whether it proves a Davidic Judahite state vs other polities/chronologies. Media often jumped from fortress → 'King David's city.' Scholarly debate ongoing. Pattern (A).
properties.sources: Garfinkel Qeiyafa excavation reports; Finkelstein critiques; BAS coverage of Qeiyafa ostracon and fortifications
properties.notes: Bible correctly points attention to Elah corridor; political label is the stretch. Surveyor type (A).

properties.name: Gath (Tell es-Safi) — 'Goliath' media overreach
properties.location: Tell es-Safi, Shephelah, Israel
properties.hypothesis: 1 Sam 17 Goliath of Gath; Philistine pentapolis. Excavation sought Philistine Gath; a pottery sherd with names resembling 'Goliath' sparked headlines implying the giant's name on site.
properties.found: Major Philistine city matching Gath's scale and destruction (likely Hazael); inscribed pottery with Indo-European-like names in the Goliath phonetic neighborhood—not an ID of the biblical giant.
properties.divergence: Maeir himself cautioned against equating the sherd with biblical Goliath. Site ID as Gath is strong; personal Goliath claim was media overreach. Pattern (A).
properties.sources: Maeir Gath project publications; BAS reports on Goliath-like inscription; Maeir public clarifications
properties.notes: Good example: Bible → right city; headline → wrong certainty. Surveyor type (A).

creation_ministry.blurb: No verified AiG article specifically cautioning “Goliath” media overreach at Tell es-Safi/Gath was found. Coverage: none_found for this contested media claim.

properties.name: Jerusalem — City of David 'palace of David' (Large Stone Structure)
properties.location: City of David ridge, Jerusalem
properties.hypothesis: 2 Sam 5: David takes Jerusalem; lives in a palace. Eilat Mazar announced Large Stone Structure as King David's palace guided by biblical topography.
properties.found: Massive stone structure and nearby Stepped Stone Structure; Iron Age pottery assemblages debated (10th vs 9th/later).
properties.divergence: Whether the building is 10th-c. royal Davidic palace remains sharply contested; alternative datings and functions proposed. Bible correctly focuses search on the southeastern hill; palace ID not settled. Pattern (A).
properties.sources: Mazar BAR articles on David's palace; Finkelstein et al. critiques in Tel Aviv / BAS; City of David excavation summaries
properties.notes: Method case: using Bible as digging guide can work for neighborhoods and still overshoot on named rooms. Surveyor type (A).
